note.text:
Science is knowledge about the natural world that we get by observing carefully, asking questions and testing our ideas with experiments.
The three main branches of science are:
• Physics: matter and energy: forces, motion, heat, light, sound, electricity.
• Chemistry: what substances are made of and how they change into new substances.
• Biology: living things: plants, animals and people.
Other branches study the Earth and the sky: Geology (rocks), Meteorology (weather) and Astronomy (planets and stars).
Science helps us in daily life: medicines, electricity, phones, clean water and better farming all come from science.

worked_example.problem: Ndi wants to know why the water in a black pot gets hot faster in the sun than the water in a white pot. Which branch of science studies this?
steps: The question is about heat, which is a form of energy.
Energy, heat, light and motion are studied in Physics.

cards.idea: Science is knowledge we get by observing, asking questions and testing ideas with experiments.
example: A farmer sees that maize grows better where there is manure. A scientist tests it: two plots, one with manure, one without.

right.text: Science is knowledge we get by observing and testing our ideas.

wrong.text: Science is a list of facts we must believe without checking.
wrong.explain: Scientists check their ideas with observations and experiments.

wrong.text: Science is only done by people in big laboratories.
wrong.explain: Anyone who observes carefully and tests ideas is doing science, even at home or on a farm.

wrong.text: Science is the same thing as magic.
wrong.explain: Science explains things by observing and testing, not by magic.

cards.idea: The three main branches: Physics (matter and energy), Chemistry (substances and how they change), Biology (living things).
example: A rolling ball: Physics. Rusting iron: Chemistry. A growing plant: Biology.

cards.idea: Other branches study the Earth and the sky: Geology (rocks), Meteorology (weather), Astronomy (planets and stars).
example: The rocks of Mount Cameroon: Geology. The rainy season: Meteorology. The Moon: Astronomy.

questions.prompt: Match each branch of science with what it studies.

pick.why: The heart is part of a living body: Biology.
Rusting changes iron into a new substance: Chemistry.

pick.t: what table salt is made of
pick.why: What substances are made of is Chemistry.
Motion and speed are part of Physics.

pick.t: how sound travels through the air
pick.why: Sound is a form of energy: Physics.
Rocks and the Earth's crust are studied in Geology.
Planets and stars are studied in Astronomy.

questions.prompt: A scientist studies {x.t}. Which branch of science is this?

misconceptions.explain: Not this branch. Think: is it about energy and motion, substances, living things, rocks, weather or the sky?

right.text: Physics, Chemistry and Biology are the three main branches of science.
Medicines, electricity and phones all came from science.
A scientist tests an idea before saying it is true.

wrong.text: Biology studies rocks and soil only.
wrong.explain: Biology studies living things. Rocks are studied in Geology.

wrong.text: Physics is the study of living things.
wrong.explain: Physics studies matter and energy. Living things are Biology.
Science gives better seeds, fertilisers and ways to fight pests.
Weather is Meteorology. Chemistry studies substances and how they change.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Meteorology helps farmers know when the rains will come.
Astronomy studies the Moon, the planets and the stars.
Chemistry studies what substances are made of.
Physics studies forces, motion, heat, light and sound.

wrong.explain: Geology studies rocks. The weather is studied in Meteorology.

wrong.text: Biology studies how a lamp makes light.
wrong.explain: Light is studied in Physics. Biology studies living things.
